name: clostridial species overview
title: Clostridia decision chart: anaerobic spore-forming Gram-positive bacilli told apart by what the patient shows: diarrhea after antibiotics (C. difficile), dying or infected tissue (C. perfringens, septicum, sordellii), spastic paralysis (tetanus) or flaccid paralysis (botulism), each with the toxin action that explains it

root.title: Gram-positive, ANAEROBIC, spore-forming bacillus: what is its TOXIN doing to the patient?
lines: spores: inactive, survive for years, hard to destroy
HARD TO CULTURE → test by PCR, or immunoassay for antigen and toxin

head: h
C. difficile
after ANTIBIOTICS kill the normal gut flora
pres: Test: nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT) for the toxin gene
or enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) for antigen + toxin · NOT culture
tox: tight junctions lost → fluid secretion, neutrophils, cell death

head: h
C. perfringens · septicum · sordellii
pres: • sordellii: toxic shock syndrome, gynecologic, soft tissue
tox: tissue breaks down and dies: greenish-black

head: h
C. tetani: TETANUS
tox: the INHIBITORY transmitters are lost → spasm

head: h
C. botulinum: BOTULISM
pres: • infant ('floppy baby'): honey under 6 months, dust, soil
tox: no muscle contraction · the most potent bacterial toxin
